records.finding: v2.3.0 (#331) ties the skill pack to platform.pin: `warden skills pin` refuses a skew, and the release notes and Releasing.md step 9 say a consumer bump re-adds the marketplace at the new tag. CONTRIBUTING's install bullet says a pin bump means reinstalling warden only and never mentions the pack. Run in this worktree, `warden skills pin` refuses: "marketplace agentops is added with no ref (source: directory), so the pack floats ... repo.yaml pins v2.3.0". A contributor following CONTRIBUTING after this bump has a warden at v2.3.0 and a skill pack at an unpinned version, and the pack is what calls .warden/bin/warden.
records.evidence: New bullet (lines 91-96) gives the pack install at the pin tag: `claude plugin marketplace add 'https://github.com/NightWatchEng/agentops#<tag>'` then `claude plugin install agentops-skills@agentops`. These are the same two commands as v2.3.0 docs/wiki/Installation.md section 3 (lines 156-157) and packpin.install_commands. The claim that 'warden skills pin refuses a machine whose installed pack is not the one platform.pin names' matches packpin.check at v2.3.0: it returns UNPINNED (exit 1) for a missing marketplace, no ref, a ref that differs from the pin, or an installed version/commit that differs from the clone. Run live here, warden 2.3.0 `skills pin` exits 1 with 'marketplace agentops is added with no ref (source: directory)... repo.yaml pins v2.3.0'. The 'remove a marketplace added from another source first' and 're-adding the marketplace at the new tag' wording agrees with Installation.md lines 179-187 ('a marketplace name refuses a changed source, so a bump is claude plugin marketplace remove agentops followed by the two lines above at the new tag') and with the remove-then-add fix string packpin prints.
